CLARES AGAINST CHANG
TSO-LIN

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Zong Yu-hsiang has issued a long circular telegram attacking Chiang Tso-in and urging him to retire.

label: text
text: Tunn Chijui Prepares to Depart.

label: text
text: Tuan Chi-jui expressed his intention of resigning, but was pressed to remain. He intends issuing a mandate stating that unless peace is restored so that the conference can continue, he will quit.

label: text
text: "Feng Yu-hsiang is expected here very shortly. Tuan Chi-jui's servants state that his belongings have been packed up, so that he can leave at a moment's notice. The Anfuite Tseng Yu-chun, who has been acting as emissary between Tuan Chi-jui and Feng-tien, was arrested at Chienmen station this afternoon on the point of leaving for Tientsin. Tseng

label: text
text: sent to Paotouchen to-night. Other Anfuites are apprehensive, fearing arrest. Wu Kuan-hsin is reported only to have escaped arrest by leaving for Tientsin yesterday.

label: text
text: Feng Yu-hsiang brought one division and one brigade from Nanyuan into Peking to-day.

label: paragraph_title
text: Governing Cabinet Suggested.

label: text
text: Tuan Chi-jui summoned another special meeting at his residence last night, which was attended by most of the members of the Cabinet. He again advocated resigning and suggested the formation of a governing Cabinet under Huang Fu, as after the coup d'état of last year. Most of those present opposed, and urged Tuan Chi-jui to remain for the sake of the conference. No decision was reached.

label: text
text: The students are arranging a big demonstration to-morrow, at which in addition to the demand for unconditional tariff autonomy, they will urge the abolition of Tupanships, placing provincial control in the hands of Civil Governors, and disbandment of superfluous troops. It is not expected that the police will prevent the demonstration.

label: text
text: Feng Yu-hsiang's third division arrived at Nanyuan from Kalgan last night. Half are remaining at Nanyuan and half proceeding to Changsintien.

label: text
text: Tuan Chi-jui has sent his aide-de-camp to see Lu Chung-lin. He said he would take personal responsibility for political suspects and requested the immediate release of Tseng Yu-chun. The latter was accordingly released on bail this morning.

label: text
text: It is understood that official circles consider Chang Tso-lin virtually eliminated unless an unexpected coup is sprung. Japan is not likely to reinforce the Manchuria garrison.

label: paragraph_title
text: Japan's Attitude.

label: paragraph_title
text: Tokyo, Nov. 27.

label: text
text: The Japanese Consult General has cabled to Tokyo for two more warships, following an emergency mass meeting of his nationals, who hold that the situation is menacing. Reports are continually arriving of banditry and looting in the interior but foreigners have apparently been unharmed, although many have come here for safety.

label: text
text: The city of Tsingtao is outwardly calm but the police have issued an ultimatum demanding four months back pay. This has alarmed the civil authorities who have ordered the Chamber of Commerce to raise the necessary $300,000.

label: text
text: ALLEGED PROMOTION SQUEEZE.

label: text
text: Holding a rank similar to that of sergeant-major, Havildar Major Chan Chu-fat, a Hakka Chinese, of the 40th Coy., Royal Engineers (native personnel) was charged before a District Court Martial (in the R.E. Theatre) at Wellington Barracks this morning with “receiving a valuable consideration in respect of a promotion.”

label: text
text:
The alleged offence related to the promotion of Lance-Naik Leung Tai to Naik (corporal).
Major J. F. Drake, 1/East Surreys, was President. Other members of the Court were Captain J. W. McCardy, R.A., and Lieut. J. H. Smith, M.C., R.A.

label: text
text: Lieut. A. J. L. Whyte, R.E., prosecuted and Mr. L. D. Turner defended

label: text
text: Corporal Gore, R.E., told the Courthastak Naik Leung Tai had complained to him about accused wanting money on the Naik's receiving a gratuity at the end of October. According to the evidence the Naik told witness that the Havildar Major would lead him a dog's life if money was not paid.

label: text
text:
Acting C.S.M. Pitt was the second witness. On November 9 he said, Naik Leung Tai reported to him that accused had demanded $50 for getting him the second stripe; that morning $20 had been paid. Witness asked the Naik if there were witnesses and the Naik replied that he had five. Accordingly, witness reported to the officer, commanding the company.

200 ANTI-REDS PUT OVER
BORDER.

label: text
text: Yesterday morning the Police completed arrangements for repatriating the detachment—over 200 strong—of anti-Red soldiers who arrived here from Amoy after being “on their last legs” through the fortunes of war.

label: text
text: As reported yesterday they were in General Chan Kwing-ming's army. A long trek into Fukien province followed defeat by the Whampor Cadets. In supposedly friendly territory they were stripped of their fighting implements. Going without food for three days, they reached Amoy and came on here.

label: text
text: ...They were taken in hand on arrival and were put across the frontier at Samehun.

text: FALL OVER WALL.

label: text
text: A sudden attack of illness is thought to have been the reason for the fall over the Praya Wall at East Point of a Chinese watchman who early yesterday morning

label: text
text: was drowned as a result. He was employed at Jardine's coal depot. Boat people in the neighbourhood were attracted by the cries of the drowning man but they got to him too late. The body was recovered. The deceased was 68 years of age.

label: paragraph_title
text: WIRELESS STRIKE

label: text
text: ACTION BY BOARD OF TRADE.

label: text
text: REGULATIONS RELAXED.

label: paragraph_title
text: London, Nov. 27.

label: text
text: The strike of wireless operators does not involved the land stations, but the Association of Wireless and Cable Telegraphists, which called the strike, claims as members 98 per cent. of the wireless operators aboard British merchantmen.

label: text
text: Wireless operators have been instructed to report to the union as ships come into port and not to sign on for fresh voyages, but ships already at sea are not endangered as existing contracts will not be broken.

label: text
text: The opinion is expressed that if the Board of Trade insists on the full observance of the regulations with regard to the carrying of wireless operators, many ships must be held up.

label: paragraph_title
text: CREATING RIDICULE?

label: text
text: London, Nov. 27.

label: text
text: The Association of Wireless and Cable Telegraphists says that approximately 200 operators up to the present have refused to renew their signatures on ships articles and asserts that one Liverpool, one Glasgow and two Hull boats have been held up.

label: text
text: The Association criticises the Board of Trade relaxation cabled earlier as a move in favour of shipowners which will create suspicion and ridicule of Government regulations.

label: text
text: The two ships held up at Hull later sailed with Board of Trade clearances.

label: text
text: It is reported from Liverpool that operators on the White Star boat "Celtic" are among those who refused to sign but the Cunard, Alfred Holt and Brocklebank lines are not affected as they employ their own operators and have not given notice of any reduction in wages.

label: text
text: An earlier cable stated: The Telegraphists Association has issued strike notices in the case of all wireless operators aboard British ships, land have instructed the men not to sign for further voyages pending a settlement of the dispute regarding conditions of service, including the proposed reduction of wages of 22s.6d. monthly.

label: paragraph_title
text: TRADE POINTS.

label: paragraph_title
text: BRITISH AND GERMAN INTERESTS.

label: text
text: CONFERENCE HITCH

label: text
text: It is semi-officially stated that negotiations between the British and German delegations on questions arising out of the Anglo-German trade agreement have been provisionally broken off owing to differences of opinion with regard to the interpretation of various points in the protocol, although understanding was reached with regard to the application of the respective customs tariffs.

label: text
text: The disagreement related to the interpretation of a clause in the protocol of the Anglo-German commercial treaty whereby the British Government pledged itself not to impose duties especially detrimental to Germany.

label: text
text: The German delegates claimed that the British customs duties on many German exports, especially musical instruments and planos, should be abrogated or considerably reduced in view of this clause.
